newsitem.title: INDIA: Prominent Indian union leader shot dead.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Indian union leader shot dead.

text.p: Well-known Indian trade union leader Datta Samant was killed by unidentified gunmen on Thursday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said.
Earlier police said Samant was shot while travelling in a car in a Bombay suburb but did not give any details.
"He was fired upon. We have no other details," one official told Reuters. Police could not confirm that he had died.
PTI said Samant was shot by assailants riding in a motor-rickshaw.
"Samant was immediately rushed to hospital...but succumbed to bullet injuries," PTI said.
Police said Samant, a former member of parliament, was shot at Powai, a Bombay suburb, at 11.24 a.m. (0554 GMT)
Samant shot into fame in the early 1980s as a fiery union leader who led a prolonged textile strike in Bombay.
Last year he led a strike at automobile maker PAL-Peugeot Ltd.
